utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, everybody, and welcome to this ninth Status Conference in the Djordjevic appeal. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-05-87/1-A, the Prosecutor versus Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. FINNIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Sarah Finnin. I appear for the Prosecution with Kyle Wood and Colin Nawrot, our Case Manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Appellant Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm the co-counsel of the accused, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I proceed any further, I just want to make sure that all parties can follow the proceedings in a language that they understand. Particularly you, Mr. Djordjevic, are you able to follow the proceedings in a language that you understand and, therefore, follow them? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. This Status Conference is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The purpose is to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. In the present case, the parties filed their Notices of Appeal on 24 May 2011 and the first Status Conference was held on 30 May 2011. The second through eighth Status Conferences were held on 21st September 2011, 16th January, 11th May, 23rd August, and 5th December, 2012, and 9th April and 17 July 2013 respectively. Today's Status Conference, being the ninth in this case, was scheduled by an order issued by myself on the 14th of October, 2013. I might as well tell you that my expectation is that this will be the last Status Conference before the delivery of judgement, and therefore, I enjoin you, if you have any matters to raise, to raise them today. Firstly, I would like to inquire into the status of the detention condition -- conditions and health situation of Mr. Djordjevic. Mr. Djordjevic, if you have any concerns in relation to the conditions of your detention or your state of health, I would invite you to raise them now, and if you prefer, this discussion can take place in private session. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Everything is all right in the Detention Unit, and I have no complaints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And on your part, Mr. Djurdjic, you have got nothing to add?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'll just give a review of the recent procedural history before we close down. As I noted at the last Status Conference, the parties have heard me summarise the procedural history many times before, and for that reason I have not included all the same details here today. However, I will again set out the dates of the most important filings and events below, as it is important that the public be made aware of the background of the case. Both the Defence and the Prosecution filed their Notices of Appeal on 24 May 2011, having previously been granted an extension of time of 60 days. The Prosecution presented two grounds of appeal, and Djordjevic presented 19 grounds of appeal. After having granted various extensions of time and word limits, the parties filed their appeal briefs on 15 August 2011, their response briefs on 26 September 2011, and their reply briefs on 26 October 2011. The Prosecution filed a public redacted version of its appeal brief on 17 August 2011, while Djordjevic filed his public redacted version of his appeal brief on 30 September 2011. However, following a confidential motion by the Prosecution requesting redactions of certain information, Djordjevic was ordered to make an additional redaction, and he refiled the public redacted version of his appeal brief on 23 January 2012. Both parties filed public redacted versions of their response briefs on 30 January 2012. The Prosecution filed its public redacted brief on 8 February 2012, and Djordjevic filed a notice of reclassification of his reply brief on 9 February 2012. On 7 March 2012, President Meron issued an order assigning Judge Khalida Rachid Khan to the Bench in place of Judge Fausto Pocar. Subsequently, on 27 September 2012, Judge Patrick Robinson was assigned to the Bench in lieu of Judge Liu Daqun. On 17 October 2012, the translation of the Trial Judgement into the B/C/S language was filed. The following day, I issued an order setting the time-limit to file any motion seeking a variation of the grounds of appeal following the translation of the Trial Judgement. Pursuant to that order, Djordjevic filed a submission on 29 November 2012. There was a further change to the Bench pursuant to an order issued by President Meron on 19 March 2013. Judge Bakhtiyar Tuzmukhamedov was assigned to the Bench in place of Judge Andresia Vaz. Finally, the appeals of the parties were heard before the full Bench on Monday, 13 May 2013. Having said all this, I would like now to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this point. Ms. Finnin.

utterances.speaker: MS. FINNIN
utterances.text: Nothing for the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I conclude this afternoon's proceedings, I would like to inform the parties that my colleagues and I on the Bench are in the final stages of the process of finalizing our judgement in this case. We are making very good progress and expect to deliver our judgement probably sometime in January. If not, it will be in early February. A Scheduling Order to that effect will be issued shortly. Unless I hear any questions or remarks, I believe that I can now conclude today's Status Conference, which I'm doing now. I thank the parties for their attendance and now adjourn these proceedings. Thank you.
